questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which ANCA-associated vasculitides are listed under small-vessel vasculitis?
questions.exp: Small-vessel vasculitis is split into immune-complex mediated and ANCA-associated; ANCA-associated examples are GPA, MPA and allergic/eosinophilic GPA. (Book p499)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: ANCA target antigens are located mainly where, and which two named antigens are listed?
opts: Basement membrane; collagen IV and elastin
Azurophilic granules of resting neutrophils more than monocyte lysosomes; PR3 and MPO
questions.exp: ANCA targets are in azurophilic granules of resting neutrophils more than lysosomes of monocytes and include PR3 and MPO. (Book p499)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: An infection trigger leads to LPS antigen exposure, neutrophil priming with PR3/MPO expression, ANCA binding, alternate complement activation, degranulation and NETosis. Which pathogenesis is this?
questions.exp: The ANCA pathogenesis flowchart starts with infection/LPS, primes neutrophils to express PR3/MPO and proceeds through ANCA, alternate complement activation, degranulation and NETosis. (Book p499)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: In the NETosis arm of ANCA pathogenesis, ineffective NET degradation ultimately does what?
opts: Increases exposure of NET components, stimulates ANCA production and attacks primed neutrophils
questions.exp: NETosis forms neutrophil extracellular traps; ineffective degradation exposes NET components, stimulates ANCA production and attacks primed neutrophils. (Book p499)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: What is the screening test for ANCA in the source?
questions.exp: The ANCA screening test shown is indirect immunofluorescence. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: A cytoplasmic ANCA pattern corresponds to which antibody and confirmatory test sequence?
opts: Anti-MPO pattern followed by no confirmation
Anti-C1q pattern confirmed by skin biopsy
Anti-PR3 pattern followed by ELISA confirmation as true c-ANCA
questions.exp: The cytoplasmic pattern is anti-PR3; confirmation is by ELISA, producing true c-ANCA positivity. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which order is printed for causes of true c-ANCA positivity?
questions.exp: True c-ANCA causes are ordered GPA > MPA > renal-limited vasculitis > EGPA. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: True p-ANCA positivity against MPO is most strongly ordered with which diseases and drug examples?
opts: Renal-limited vasculitis > MPA > EGPA > GPA; hydralazine, PTU, levamisole-adulterated cocaine and minocycline
questions.exp: True p-ANCA against MPO is ordered renal-limited vasculitis > MPA > EGPA > GPA and includes drug-induced hydralazine, PTU, levamisole-adulterated cocaine and minocycline. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which condition is listed under false p-ANCA positivity rather than true p-ANCA against MPO?
questions.exp: False p-ANCA causes include autoimmune hepatitis type 1, primary sclerosing cholangitis, RA, IBD, infective endocarditis and cystic fibrosis. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: What skin biopsy/immunofluorescence note is printed for ANCA vasculitis?
opts: IgA deposits are mandatory in every ANCA case
Biopsy is contraindicated in all vasculitis
Biopsy and immunofluorescence of skin are most preferred, with no deposits indicating pauci-immune disease
questions.exp: Biopsy and immunofluorescence of skin are marked most preferred; no deposits indicate pauci-immune disease. (Book p500)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which cutaneous lesion is called the hallmark feature of ANCA vasculitis?
questions.exp: ANCA cutaneous palpable purpura is labelled non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura and hallmark feature. (Book p501)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: A skin lesion is pinpoint, non-blanchable and due to capillary inflammation. Which source term fits?
questions.exp: Petechiae are described as non-blanchable pinpoint macules due to capillary inflammation. (Book p501)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which table pairing is correct for small-vessel vasculitis in skin?
opts: Large vessels, bruits and pulse/BP asymmetry only
Dermal veins, oral ulcers and hypopyon only
Capillaries/post-capillary venules, superficial capillary dermis, purpura-petechiae-bulla-urticaria
Muscular arteries, reticular dermis, deep ulcers and mononeuritis multiplex
questions.exp: Small-vessel involvement is capillaries and post-capillary venules in superficial capillary dermis with purpura, petechiae, bulla and urticaria. (Book p501)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: Which features in the table point to medium-vessel vasculitis rather than small-vessel disease?
opts: Nodules, gangrene, mononeuritis multiplex and deep ulcers
questions.exp: Medium-vessel vasculitis involves muscular arteries in the reticular dermis and features nodules, gangrene, mononeuritis multiplex and deep ulcers. (Book p501)

questions.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
questions.q: ANCA titres are noted as a predictor of what?
questions.exp: The page states ANCA titres are a predictor of relapse. (Book p501)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which feature combination defines GPA in the printed source?
opts: Necrotising vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis and granuloma
Necrotising vasculitis without granuloma and ANCA negative
questions.exp: GPA features include necrotising vasculitis plus fibrinoid necrosis due to neutrophils plus granuloma. (Book p501)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which antibody and demographic pattern is printed for GPA?
opts: c-ANCA about 70% greater than p-ANCA about 25%, age group over 40, male equals female
questions.exp: GPA lists c-ANCA 70% > p-ANCA 25%, age group >40 years, sex M=F and HLA DPB1 04. (Book p501)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Upper respiratory tract involvement in GPA is printed as what frequency and key manifestation?
opts: Rare involvement with no nasal disease
95% involvement with midline nasal deformities such as saddle nose
questions.exp: GPA major manifestations list upper respiratory tract involvement in 95% with midline nasal deformities, including septal ulcers/crusting/perforation and saddle nose deformity. (Book p502)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which GPA lower respiratory pattern is printed?
opts: 90% involvement with thick-walled cavitating nodules and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Interstitial lung disease as the only chest imaging sign
Pulmonary artery aneurysm as the universal sign
questions.exp: Lower respiratory involvement in GPA is 90%, with thick-walled cavitating nodules and DAH. (Book p502)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: GPA renal involvement is described how?
opts: Renal artery stenosis with no glomerulonephritis
60% with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, type 3 RPGN and pauci-immune pattern
Rare renal disease with hyperviscosity only
questions.exp: Renal involvement in GPA is 60%; RPGN is type 3 and pauci-immune. (Book p502)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which minor manifestation set belongs to GPA?
opts: Painless oral ulcers with genital scarring
Arthralgia, peripheral neuropathy, cutaneous non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura, scleritis/orbital pseudotumour/rare lacrimal involvement
Only erosive DIP arthritis and tophi
questions.exp: GPA minor systemic manifestations include joints arthralgia, CNS peripheral neuropathy, skin palpable purpura and ocular scleritis, orbital pseudotumour and rare lacrimal involvement. (Book p502)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Thick-walled cavitating nodules on chest imaging have which printed differential list?
opts: SLE, dermatomyositis, Caplan syndrome and CPPD
Wegener granulomatosis, lung SCC, histoplasmosis and lung abscess
questions.exp: The note lists thick-walled cavitating nodules in Wegener granulomatosis, SCC of lung, histoplasmosis and lung abscess. (Book p503)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which profile is printed for microscopic polyangiitis?
opts: Elderly 50–65 years, males more than females, necrotising fibrinoid vasculitis with no granuloma, p-ANCA > c-ANCA
Children, IgA deposition and abdominal colic only
questions.exp: MPA is described in elderly 50–65 years, male>female, necrotising vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis but no granuloma, and p-ANCA > c-ANCA. (Book p503)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which MPA organ-frequency statement is printed?
opts: Lower respiratory tract 50% with DAH, upper respiratory tract 30% sinusitis, renal 100% with type 3 RPGN
Upper respiratory tract 95% with saddle nose and renal 60%
Pulmonary infiltrates absent and renal rare
questions.exp: MPA lists lower respiratory 50% DAH, upper respiratory 30% sinusitis and renal 100%, most commonly RPGN type 3. (Book p503)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which minor manifestation pattern favors MPA in the source?
opts: CNS severe cranial neuropathy is universal
Ocular unlikely, joint not significant, skin more common than GPA, CNS minimal neuropathy
Ocular scleritis most common with orbital pseudotumour
questions.exp: MPA minor manifestations are ocular unlikely, joints not significant, skin more common than GPA and CNS minimal neuropathy. (Book p503)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which induction regimen is printed as DOC for GPA and MPA?
opts: Topical steroid plus PGE2 gel only
Methylprednisolone IV 500 mg–1 g for 3 days then oral 1 mg/kg/day tapered over 2–3 months to 5 mg/day plus cyclophosphamide
questions.exp: Induction shows methylprednisolone IV 500 mg–1 g for 3 days, then oral 1 mg/kg/day tapering over 2–3 months to 5 mg/day, plus cyclophosphamide as DOC. (Book p504)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: When is rituximab placed in GPA/MPA management?
opts: If unwilling for cyclophosphamide or used in relapse
Only as first-line for minimal disease without steroids
questions.exp: Rituximab is shown as an alternative if unwilling for cyclophosphamide and is used in relapse. (Book p504)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which minimal-disease and maintenance regimens are printed for GPA/MPA?
opts: Minimal disease: no treatment; maintenance: colchicine
Minimal disease: steroid plus methotrexate; maintenance: low-dose steroid plus azathioprine
Minimal disease: plasma exchange alone; maintenance: acyclovir
Minimal disease: sulfasalazine; maintenance: hydroxychloroquine only
questions.exp: Minimal disease is treated with steroid plus methotrexate; maintenance is low-dose steroid plus azathioprine. (Book p504)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which plasma-exchange indication list is printed for GPA/MPA?
opts: Isolated skin purpura without systemic disease
Ongoing DAH, serum creatinine >5.5 mg/dL and CNS involvement
questions.exp: Plasma exchange indications are ongoing DAH, serum creatinine >5.5 mg/dL and CNS involvement. (Book p504)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: Which GPA classification score item has the highest positive value in the printed table?
opts: Conductive or sensorineural hearing loss at +1
cANCA or anti-PR3 ANCA positive at +5
questions.exp: In the GPA table, cANCA or anti-PR3 ANCA positive scores +5, higher than +3 or +2 items. (Book p504)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: What total score and test characteristics are printed for GPA classification?
questions.exp: For GPA, total score of ≥5 is needed, with sensitivity 93% and specificity 94%. (Book p505)

questions.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
questions.q: In the MPA classification table, which item is a negative score?
questions.exp: The MPA table assigns eosinophil count ≥1×10^9/L a score of -4; pANCA/MPO is +6, pauci-immune GN +3 and fibrosis/ILD +3. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Churg-Strauss syndrome is also named which disease in the source?
opts: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis or allergic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
questions.exp: Churg-Strauss syndrome is AKA eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and allergic granulomatosis with polyangiitis. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which EGPA feature set is printed?
opts: Panarteritis without granuloma and ANCA negative only
IgA vasculitis in children below 5 years
Large-vessel granulomatous arteritis in age over 50
Necrotising vasculitis, fibrinoid necrosis, extravascular granuloma, eosinophilic, predominantly ANCA negative
questions.exp: EGPA features include necrotising vasculitis, fibrinoid necrosis, extravascular granuloma, eosinophilic disease and predominantly ANCA-negative status; ANCA positivity is bad prognosis. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which manifestations belong to the asthmatic phase of EGPA?
opts: Adolescent onset, recurrent allergic rhinitis plus asthma and migratory lung infiltrations on CXR
Eosinophilic myocarditis and cranial neuropathy only
questions.exp: The asthmatic phase is seen in adolescents and includes recurrent allergic rhinitis plus asthma and migratory lung infiltrations in CXR. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which manifestations belong to the vasculitic phase of EGPA?
opts: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis, eosinophilic myocarditis and severe neuropathy that can involve cranial nerves
Only saddle nose deformity and septal perforation
questions.exp: The vasculitic phase includes eosinophilic gastroenteritis, eosinophilic myocarditis as the most common cause of death, and severe neuropathy including cranial nerves. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: High-titre ANCA-positive EGPA cases are printed with which manifestations and prognosis?
opts: DAH, RPGN, mononeuritis multiplex possibly involving medium vessels, predominant skin lesions and bad prognosis
Only oral ulcers with good prognosis
questions.exp: High-titre ANCA-positive cases have DAH, RPGN, mononeuritis multiplex that may involve medium vessels, predominant skin lesions and bad prognosis. (Book p505)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which ACR criterion list belongs to EGPA?
opts: Weight loss >4 kg, HBV and arteriographic abnormality only
Asthma, eosinophilia >10%, mono/polyneuropathy, migratory pulmonary infiltrates, paranasal sinus abnormality and extravascular eosinophils on biopsy
questions.exp: ACR criteria for EGPA are asthma, eosinophilia >10%, mono/polyneuropathy, migratory pulmonary infiltrates, paranasal sinus abnormality and extravascular eosinophils on biopsy. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which EGPA treatment is printed?
opts: Steroid plus antiviral plus plasma exchange for all
questions.exp: EGPA treatment lists steroid plus IL-5 antagonist mepolizumab. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which pathology profile defines PAN on the page?
opts: Transmural necrotising inflammation without granuloma, neutrophil predominant, focal segmental necrosis and ANCA negative
questions.exp: PAN is described as transmural necrotising inflammation without granuloma, neutrophil predominant, focal and segmental necrosis and ANCA negative. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which PAN association is printed as the 30/1 rule?
opts: Hepatitis B: 30% of PAN cases have HBV and 1% of HBV cases have PAN
questions.exp: The PAN association note states Hepatitis B 30/1 rule: 30% of PAN cases have hepatitis B and 1% of hepatitis B cases have PAN. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which investigation is associated with PAN aneurysms/microaneurysms?
questions.exp: Aneurysms/microaneurysms in PAN are linked to conventional angiography as the investigation. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which systemic manifestation list fits PAN?
opts: Weight loss/fever/myalgia as first constitutional symptom; nodules, ulcers, gangrene; hemoptysis; renal failure with abdominal pain; testicular pain; mononeuritis multiplex
Saddle nose, recurrent epistaxis and serous otitis media only
Universal palpable purpura in children below 5
questions.exp: PAN systemic manifestations include constitutional symptoms as first symptom, nodules/ulcers/gangrene, hemoptysis, renal failure from renal artery stenosis with abdominal pain, testicular pain and mononeuritis multiplex. (Book p506)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which danger signs are printed for PAN?
opts: Abdominal pain from mesenteric vasculitis, renal artery stenosis and CNS vasculitis
questions.exp: PAN danger signs are abdominal pain due to mesenteric vasculitis, renal artery stenosis and CNS vasculitis. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which finding argues against a diagnosis of PAN because it reflects capillary involvement?
questions.exp: Findings against PAN due to capillary involvement include DAH, RPGN, petechiae, purpura, bulla, ecchymosis, ENT/ocular manifestations, asthma, positive ANCA and cryoglobulinemia. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which item is part of ACR criteria for PAN?
questions.exp: ACR criteria for PAN include weight loss >4 kg, livedo reticularis, testicular pain/tenderness, mono/polyneuropathy, diastolic BP >90, elevated BUN/creatinine, HBV, arteriographic abnormality and polymorphonuclear neutrophils on biopsy. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Cutaneous PAN is described how?
opts: Cutaneous involvement with small arteries/arterioles, venules spared and non-progressive
questions.exp: Cutaneous PAN involves small arteries/arterioles, spares venules and is non-progressive. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which PAN investigation sequence is printed?
opts: Pathergy test first and ELISA DOC
MR angiogram first investigation and conventional angiography DOC
Doppler halo sign first and temporal biopsy DOC
Synovial fluid count first and MRI contraindicated
questions.exp: PAN investigation lists MR angiogram as first investigation and conventional angiography as DOC. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which pediatric note is printed for PAN-like disease?
opts: ADA-2 deficiency in children resembles PAN
questions.exp: The note states ADA-2 deficiency in children resembles PAN. (Book p507)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: How does the source split PAN treatment by hepatitis B status?
opts: HBV positive: no therapy; HBV negative: antiviral only
HBV positive: rituximab only; HBV negative: acyclovir
HBV positive: steroid plus antiviral plus plasma exchange with good prognosis; HBV negative: steroid plus cyclophosphamide with poor prognosis
questions.exp: The treatment flowchart gives hepatitis B positive as steroid, antiviral and plasma exchange with good prognosis, and negative as steroid plus cyclophosphamide with poor prognosis. (Book p508)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: In the ANCA-vasculitis differential table, which comment is attached to Churg-Strauss syndrome?
opts: Asthma/eosinophilia and prominent peripheral nervous system involvement
Progressive renal failure is commonest in PAN
Skin purpura is absent in CSS
questions.exp: The table comments note asthma and eosinophilia in CSS and peripheral nervous system involvement often prominent in CSS. (Book p508)

questions.sec: EGPA and PAN
questions.q: Which table pattern favors Wegener granulomatosis over PAN?
opts: Pulmonary infiltrates/nodules, alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis are present; ENT disease usually favors WG
Pulmonary infiltrates absent, glomerulonephritis absent and ENT absent
Only CNS involvement without airway or renal disease
questions.exp: The differential table shows WG with high pulmonary infiltrates/nodules, alveolar hemorrhage, glomerulonephritis and upper airway disease; the comment says ENT disease usually favors WG. (Book p508)

units.title: 1. ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
units.sec: ANCA biology, testing and skin-vessel clinical framework
units.guide:
Small-vessel vasculitis splits into immune-complex and ANCA-associated arms.
ANCA targets, antibody-mediated injury, IIF/ELISA patterns and pauci-immune biopsy are kept in sequence.
Cutaneous signs and small-versus-medium-versus-large vessel features then set up GPA/MPA.

units.title: 2. GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
units.sec: GPA and MPA manifestations, management and classification
units.guide:
GPA pathology, antibody pattern and organ involvement precede CXR/CT notes.
MPA contrasts with GPA by age, sex, no granuloma, p-ANCA predominance and 100% renal disease.
Induction, maintenance, plasma exchange and classification scoring are kept as book-study algorithms.

units.title: 3. EGPA and PAN
units.guide:
Churg-Strauss/EGPA features, phases, criteria and treatment are followed by PAN pathology.
PAN associations, systemic manifestations, danger signs, exclusion clues, ACR criteria and investigations remain source ordered.
HBV-based treatment and the ANCA-vasculitis differential table close the chapter.
